post.description:
Register the calling device's identity.

A device cannot sign with a registered key before it has one, so this
route checks two other things instead:

- the request is signed with the very key being registered, which proves
  the caller holds the private key;
- the enrollment proof, which proves the caller knows the account root
  key. A stolen session token cannot produce it.

Args:
    request: The device's ID, public key, encrypted name and proof.
    http_request: The request, for its signature.
    owner: The verified account.
    devices: Where devices are kept.
    recovery: Where the account's enrollment public key is kept.

Returns:
    The registered device.

Raises:
    DeviceAuthorizationError: If the signature or the proof is not valid.
    ProblemError: 409 if the account has no keys yet, or the device ID is
        already registered.

post.description:
Revoke a device so that nothing it sends is accepted again.

The request must be signed by one of the account's devices, and the
session must show that the password was entered in the last few minutes:
someone who picks up an unlocked device cannot revoke the owner's others.
A device may revoke itself. A revoked device ID can never be used again.

Args:
    device_id: The device to revoke.
    http_request: The request, for the application's clock.
    caller: The verified account and device.
    devices: Where devices are kept.

Returns:
    The device with ``revoked_at`` set.

Raises:
    ProblemError: 403 if the password was not entered recently; 404 if
        the device is not one of the caller's, whether or not it exists
        on another account.

put.description:
Create or rotate the wrapped root key with compare-and-swap.

``expected_version`` 0 creates the envelope and fails if one exists. Any
other value replaces exactly that version. A failed attempt changes
nothing, so an interrupted rotation leaves the old recovery key valid.

Creating the envelope happens before the account has any device, so it
needs only the session. Replacing it must be signed by one of the
account's devices: a stolen session token alone cannot swap the envelope
and lock the user out of recovery.

Args:
    request: The new envelope and the version it replaces.
    http_request: The request, for its device signature.
    owner: The verified caller.
    store: Where envelopes are kept.

Returns:
    The envelope as stored, with its new version.

Raises:
    ProblemError: 409 if the stored version is not the expected one.

409.description: The envelope is not at the expected version

get.description:
Return the caller's records that changed after ``cursor``.

Each record appears once, as it is now, in the order of its latest
change, deleted records included. Ask again with ``next_cursor`` while
``has_more`` is true. When a device reaches the end of the feed, the
time is recorded as its last sync.

A cursor this account was never given is refused with
``sync.cursor_unknown``: start again from ``0``.

Args:
    caller: The verified account and device.
    store: Where records are kept.
    devices: Where the device's last sync is recorded.
    cursor: The caller's position in its change feed.

Returns:
    One page of changes.

Raises:
    ProblemError: 409 when the cursor was never issued to this account.

post.description:
Apply an idempotent batch of record operations.

Each operation is applied on its own, in request order: one that is
refused does not stop the others. A change is stored only when it was
made on top of the record's current revision. The server never merges
and never lets the latest writer win. Sending an operation that was
already applied again changes nothing and reports ``duplicate``.

A batch is not all-or-nothing. If the request fails part-way, the
operations already applied stay applied, and sending the batch again
reports them as ``duplicate``.

The payloads are opaque: they are stored as sent and never decoded.

Args:
    request: The batch to apply.
    caller: The verified account and device.
    store: Where records are kept.

Returns:
    One result per operation, in request order.
